Source-of-truth inventory

2nd Chance Housing, Inc. Researcher training · Draft for organizational and counsel review · Statutes and official pages last read 10/29/2026 · Not legal advice.

Compiled 10/29/2026 by reading the page's source (site/staff/deeds/transfer/index.html, last changed 10/28/2026) and the 10/28/2026 review package. The page was not clicked through live (it needs a staff sign-in). The live site could differ from this copy.

1. In the system (read in the page's code)

  • Case list, new case (kind: owner died, heir needs the deed), delete; per-case access list; save, saved, unsaved, error and conflict bar; version checks that refuse a stale save; History (who changed what).
  • Property card (title, address, PINs, county, legal description, owner of record, decedent, date of death); Title search at the recorder; Route evaluation with a title answer per PIN and a contradiction check.
  • Death certificate: upload and typed fields (name, birth, place of death, county, address, marital status, spouse, number, issue date, informant, copies, last four of SSN); name-difference warning; county warning if not Cook.
  • Heirs with a row each (relationship, living, address, adult, survived, agrees, can sign, notice status, tracking, mailing receipt, signed return receipt), heirs list marked complete, draft affidavit, petition worksheet with Exhibit A, certified-mail envelopes.
  • Plan facts, name check, search log, administrator eligibility, assets and bond estimate, creditors, HFS box, documents tracker (folders A, B and C; status Not started to Filed; scans; where the original is kept; a replaced scan is kept and flagged for re-check).
  • Steps with status and target dates, a preparation calendar, consultation log (Scheduled, Accepted, Needs changes first, Declined, Go to next), four readiness lists, counsel packet print, daily deadline reminder emails (per the review package).

2. Described elsewhere but not in the system

  • Automatic reading of the death certificate. The page does not read it. The instructor walkthrough at /probate-help/walkthrough/ says it does (“Upload the certificate, let the page read it”). That slide, and its audio, are inaccurate.
  • Filling the official court forms, or exporting an approved-documents bundle with a manifest (open items V16 and R12 in the review package).
  • Redacted copies of uploaded scans and retention rules; before and after values in the history (V20); a complete model of successive deaths and deeper family trees; per-route filing steps beyond checklists for heirship-only, summary administration and the title-company route.

3. Manual tasks (outside the system)

  • Finding leads, consent, interviews, searching the recorder and the court's records, ordering records, reading and typing the certificate, second-person review, the evidence index, originals register, unresolved-issues sheet, cover memo, the lead log, and tracking counsel's approval.

4. Known defects and unsupported scenarios

  • Tested with a stub page and stub database, not a real browser or staging database (review package, “Known limits”).
  • Cook County only. The page warns if she lived elsewhere.
  • Built around the four-child intestate case; fractional interests are supported only as share text and a check that shares add to 1.
  • Bond rule: Cook Rule 12.5(a) is described, an estimate only; the personal-estate bond (Probate Act) is not computed.
  • The page's statements about the filing fee, transfer-tax exemption and Medicaid protected amount were not independently confirmed for this course.

5. Decisions reserved

  • Counsel: the route; who the legal heirs are and their shares; who may serve; petition contents; notice method; whether a deed is proper; fees and scope.
  • The court: declaring heirship, appointing a representative, independent or supervised administration, bond amount.
  • The title company: whether it insures without letters, and on what terms.
